subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should OpenClaw land the scoped embedded sessions_spawn mitigation now while keeping this issue open for gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native follow-ups, or hold for one shared work-spawning policy seam?
rationale: The bug is real enough to keep open, but the active fix intentionally leaves several spawn-capable surfaces outside its mechanical guard, so automation should not decide the product scope alone.

options.title: Land Scoped Mitigation
options.body: Accept the embedded sessions_spawn guard as a partial fix and keep this issue open for the remaining surfaces.

options.title: Harden More Surfaces First
options.body: Require the candidate PR to cover gateway loopback, sessions_send/cron, or shared completion text before merge.

options.title: Pause For Shared Policy
options.body: Hold the candidate PR until maintainers choose a single policy seam spanning OpenClaw tools and Codex-native delegation.

recommendation.title: Land Scoped Mitigation
recommendation.body: Accept the embedded sessions_spawn guard as a partial fix and keep this issue open for the remaining surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the cross-harness scope review and has recent fallback-area history, making him the clearest owner for the scope decision.
